name: Blanquism
summary: Blanquism is the revolutionary tradition of Louis Auguste Blanqui: a small, disciplined and secret group seizes power in an insurrection and rules as a temporary dictatorship that suppresses counter-revolution and spreads universal secular education, until an enlightened people can govern itself under communism by association. It is atheist and fiercely anticlerical, egalitarian, hostile to class cooperation, and voluntarist, relying on conscious will rather than economic determinism.
scope: The profile represents Blanqui's own program and the conspiratorial insurrectionary method later labelled Blanquism, drawing on Communism, the Future of Society (1869), Social Wealth Must Belong to Those Who Created It (1834) and Instructions for an Armed Uprising. It excludes the later Blanquist Central Revolutionary Committee under Vaillant and the Boulangist split, and treats Engels' caricature of putschism as a critique, not as Blanqui's self-description. Many modern issues were never addressed, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Healthcare is never discussed; a communist order that protects workers from the gutter and brings goods under state control would plausibly guarantee it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage law is discussed; his early post-revolution measures fix workers' existing salaries, so he favored protecting pay, though his aim was abolishing capital rather than adjusting wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He holds that owners of capital take what workers produce and that market logic treats abundance as a disaster, so markets are the problem rather than the solution.

public-ownership.rationale: Enemy property (church, congregations) passes to state control and communism through association is the goal, which implies common ownership of major industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Communism, the Future of Society proposes replacing existing taxes with a direct progressive tax on inheritance and income.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not discussed, but he wanted workers' associations prepared and supported, which an adherent would extend to workers' organization generally.

property-fundamental.rationale: He denies that property rights may override the right to life and calls land ownership a product of force and fraud.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Early measures would force heads of industry to keep their workforce and salaries or be expelled, showing a willingness to compel owners; detailed regulation is not discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not discussed; since he insisted workers must not be left suffering after the revolution, cutting welfare as dependency-forming does not fit his outlook.

worker-ownership.rationale: He calls association "the great path towards and the last word of communism" and wants workers' associations prepared by a dedicated assembly.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; as a lifelong conspirator hunted by the police, a Blanquist would distrust state surveillance, though a revolutionary dictatorship might use it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The issue never arose; sources note his austere, rationalist outlook but give no basis for a side.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; he would restrict clerical and reactionary propaganda but there is no evidence on speech law as such.

strong-leader.rationale: The model is a temporary dictatorship seized by a small group that would act without waiting for popular consent or parliamentary process.

state-harmful.rationale: He calls government and taxation forms of communism in its worst form yet "of an absolute necessity", and uses state power to bring communism about.

limit-guns.rationale: He calls for arming workers and republicans and "general armament" to protect the revolution, so strict limits on gun ownership would contradict it.

empower-police-military.rationale: He opposed a standing army (Ni Dieu ni Maitre) and proposed disbanding the army and dissolving the magistracy, though the new order would keep its own armed force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; the Kingston archive notes his sexism but no source gives a view on sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: He proposed a Parisian dictatorship on the claim that Paris represents the nation, a centralizing Jacobin stance.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from his faith in education and from replacing the magistracy with arbitrators and juries; penal policy itself is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: He did not address the family as an institution; his anticlericalism and hostility to inherited obligations point one way, his reported sexism the other.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in any source consulted; anticlericalism argues one way, no evidence on bodily autonomy the other.

more-religion-public.rationale: His slogan is "Abolish religion, expel the priests!", and he regards the clergy as the chief enemy.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from his commitment to equality as the first law of the new order; race is not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; he stressed education forming people but the archive notes his sexism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The archive notes his nationalism and Jacobin patriotism, but cultural preservation as such is not stated.

gradual-change.rationale: Blanquism is defined by an insurrectionary seizure of power rather than gradual reform within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is never discussed; his nationalism and his egalitarianism pull in opposite directions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; his patriotism suggests wariness but his communism was universal in aim.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from his critique of market logic and capital; trade policy is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: His paper La Patrie en danger and the nationalism noted by the Kingston archive suggest national priority, but he never framed this as against cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; no source states a view on foreign intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; he aimed at universal communism but worked within a national Parisian frame.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits were not an issue; he focused on who owns wealth, not how much is produced.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; a state-directed communist order could act drastically but nothing is stated.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He placed hope in education and reason, not technology, and his Eternity by the Stars is pessimistic about history.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources applies.

revolution-justified.rationale: Instructions for an Armed Uprising is a manual for insurrection and Blanqui devoted his life to it.

experts-over-public.rationale: He wanted an enlightened leadership but also universal education so that all could judge for themselves; expert rule over the public is not his aim.

central-planning.rationale: He focused on seizing power and rarely described a finished economy, but state control of enemy property and association implies deliberate economic direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: He did not describe market arrangements; association points toward worker ownership but markets are not discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed; he proposed a progressive inheritance and income tax instead.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He proposes a direct progressive tax on inheritance and, in 1834, argues that wealth of heirless rich reverting to the state benefits the country.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; a state that fixes workers' pay differs from an unconditional payout.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from state control of enemy property and a National Savings Bank; investment steering is not stated.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He rejects dividing property among individuals as letting inequality re-emerge, though he would respect small landowners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He wants equality through association replacing individual property, which implies the end of wage dependence, but he never says money should go.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He proposed a state National Savings Bank and abolishing the public debt ledger, not leaving money to markets.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He treated owners and workers as in organized war, so state-recognized joint bodies would be a false peace.

one-party-rule.rationale: A conspiratorial group would hold power in a temporary dictatorship; whether a party leads the state afterward is not stated.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He condemns perpetual dynasties and fought for the Republic.

democracy-best.rationale: In 1848 he called for indefinite postponement of elections, which cuts against treating democracy as best regardless of outcome.

direct-votes.rationale: He wanted elections postponed until the people were enlightened, so direct votes on laws would be premature.

workers-councils.rationale: His model is a Parisian dictatorship and a national assembly, not council power; councils did not exist in his time.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from his Jacobin centralism and claim that Paris represents the nation.

natural-rulers.rationale: He insists equality is the first law of the new order and that education protects everyone from deception.

political-violence-never.rationale: His Instructions for an Armed Uprising organizes a military insurrection and he devoted his life to insurrection.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not stated; he opposed the government's war effort in 1870 while backing national defense.

separate-church-state.rationale: He rejects any church budget and wants priests expelled, going well beyond separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He wants religion abolished and calls the clergy the chief enemy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He would dissolve the magistracy in favor of public arbitrators and juries and replace the army with a national army.

military-superiority.rationale: He opposed a standing army; superiority over rivals is not his concern.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His patriotism is Jacobin and republican rather than ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He describes society as split between victors and vanquished in organised war, but he rejected historical determinism, so this is not his theory of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He writes that equality is the foundation and first law of the new order and that no one will tolerate unequal wealth once enlightened.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights were not a 19th-century French revolutionary concern; none of his texts takes a side.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources consulted.

civilizational-union.rationale: His loyalty was to the French republic and its revolutionary tradition.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He condemns the idle minority living on others' labour and aims at association.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He worked in the Rousseauian tradition of the general will and collective participation, which subordinates individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Blanqui's texts concern class power and education, with no discussion of nature's value apart from humans.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; he attributed poverty to social institutions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He saw bourgeois society as hell on earth, but his target was capitalism and not industry as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: His program is about seizing power and educating the people, with no stance on pace of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources applies.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from his stress on conscious collective will and education.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: His method relied on a secret conspiratorial organization, so secrecy against state authorities fits.

restore-past-order.rationale: He argues each generation should not bind the next and sees the Middle Ages as barbarism under Christianity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He held that political action must be driven by conscious purpose and ideas, not by pragmatic outcomes.

direct-action.rationale: Blanquism is putschism, relying on an armed coup rather than elections; he even sought to postpone elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: A secret minority seizing power by force to bring about a free society is the opposite of means mirroring ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He sought communism as civilization's necessary outcome through education, not a return to prehistory.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He opposed professional schools confining workers to a trade, which hints at the idea, but does not call for abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from equality as the first law and care for workers; no explicit distribution formula is stated.

production-for-use.rationale: He criticizes the market logic in which low prices and abundance harm producers and capital withdraws when profits fall.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He argues capital has value only through labour and owners therefore take what workers produce.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He proposed a temporary Parisian dictatorship against counter-revolution, but one led by a revolutionary minority rather than the working class as such.

collective-farming.rationale: He would respect small and medium landowners, make collectives voluntary and thought peasants hard to win over.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not discussed; he described class conflict, not interstate war, as the result.

taxation-theft.rationale: He calls taxation a form of communism, albeit in its worst form and absolutely necessary, and proposes progressive direct taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from his state-led program of compulsory education and expelling the clergy.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He worked in a Rousseauian collective-will tradition.

conscription.rationale: He wanted a national army and general armament of the people, which implies universal service, though conscription is not named.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from his republican insistence on collective political action.

state-as-business.rationale: He opposes market logic and treats the state as the instrument of communism.

positive-liberty.rationale: He writes that equality is the limit to freedom and that freedom requires education and communism.

media-academia-power.rationale: He believed church and press held great power but did not address universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: His faith in education and equality is incompatible with innate hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: He would rely on a revolutionary committee and later a national assembly.

total-state.rationale: He said the state should not impose communism suddenly and that joining collectives would be voluntary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; revolution was to regenerate society but not framed as national decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; his patriotism was defensive.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He relied on an oath to the Republic and a commander chosen in advance, a republican chain of command, not feudal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: He holds that workers are dependent on owners as a result of force and fraud and wants equality.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He distinguished clerical indoctrination from rational instruction, which implies knowledge can be free of power, but no explicit stance exists.

universal-morality.rationale: The archive places him in the Rousseauian Enlightenment tradition; moral universalism is not stated.

single-common-good.rationale: He worked within the Rousseauian idea of a general will and a free society of equals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism postdates his political activity and he never addressed a Jewish state.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in any text of his or in the scholarship on Blanquism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a Blanquist theme; no source records a position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Association is his path to communism, with workers' associations prepared by an assembly.

school-vouchers.rationale: He opposes independent schools because they would hand education to the Jesuits and demands free compulsory secular state schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He proposed abolishing the public debt ledger but did not discuss deficit policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: He sees economic freedom of owners as organised war on workers, so political freedom depends on ending it.

rule-by-example.rationale: He relied on military discipline and a hierarchy of command and a dictatorship, not moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: His patriotism and republicanism suggest support, but it is not stated.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN is anachronistic; his only recorded foreign-policy stance is patriotic national defense in 1870.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The archive says he held that philosophy rules the world and stressed reasoned common purpose, and he was an atheist.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility rules for immigrants are not discussed; his writings address workers as a class.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; idle owners are condemned but welfare rules are not discussed.

class-collaboration.rationale: He saw society as a war to the death between classes and rejected class cooperation and the middle way.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He prized education and instruction, so destroying libraries and museums would contradict his program.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc of states against Western powers is anachronistic and outside his French republican frame.

workers-nation.rationale: His patriotic Jacobin outlook suggests national organization, but he also called for working-class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The archive notes his sexism but no source states his legal view.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest on loans is never addressed; his financial proposals concern the public debt ledger and a savings bank.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts equality as the first law of the new order.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He argues that law made property the foundation of social order, so the state serves owners until overthrown.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy of this kind is anachronistic for a mid-19th-century revolutionary.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not discussed; Jacobin universalism and national patriotism pull both ways.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian universalism; unlikely to hold conspiracy theories about immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; he wanted elections postponed after a revolution.

national-mission.rationale: Jacobin heirs saw France as a revolutionary vanguard, but he did not state it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The archive notes his sexism; no view is recorded.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He sees the ruling order as an idle minority that gathers up everything produced by workers.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of innate hierarchy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He campaigned for a general pardon of Communards and suffered state repression, but accountability is not stated.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wants a state that takes over enemy property, runs mass schooling and prepares association.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality is the foundation of his political thought.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He aimed to begin in Paris, which would represent the nation; international spread is not discussed.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as an analytic category is not found in his writings.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from his demand for one secular system and the end of clerical privilege.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He wanted religion abolished through expulsion of clergy and education, not conversion rules.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He demands free, compulsory, secular schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: He foresaw a counter-revolution needing a strong state and general armament; encirclement as such is anachronistic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His dictatorship postponed consent until people were enlightened, while his goal was a self-governing people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are not discussed in his economic writings.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He organized armed uprisings against the government.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He builds communism on association rather than rivalry and held class war a evil to be ended.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The archive places him in the republican free-society-of-equals tradition.

separated-powers.rationale: He proposed concentrated Parisian dictatorship and dissolution of the magistracy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Blanquism holds that a small, highly organised and secretive group should lead revolution instead of relying on mass movements.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He insists workers not be left in the gutter after revolution.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of individual property as the remedy.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from his side in the class war.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He attributes workers' misery to property and the owners' power, not numbers.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: He favored appointed command and commissions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His temporary dictatorship exists to suppress counter-revolution.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He criticizes market pricing and supports state intervention.

party-controls-media.rationale: He decried the controlled press of the old order; the new order's media policy is not stated.

party-commands-army.rationale: The insurrectionary force obeys a commander-in-chief of the conspirators; later arrangements are not stated.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in any source consulted.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from his hostility to the idle rich and commitment to equality.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Volunteers swear to obey leaders' orders and no movement occurs without the commander-in-chief's order.

church-by-bishops.rationale: He wanted the clergy expelled and the church stripped of budget.

clerical-rule.rationale: He calls the clergy a black army spreading ignorance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In 1870 his paper La Patrie en danger attacked the government for weak war effort, wanting to defend France.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He cared about clerical education and press control but left no view on censoring art for moral reasons.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of perpetual dynasties and each generation binding the next.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Permanent military alliances are not discussed; he opposed a standing army but said nothing on treaties.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: He did not favor individual property as the answer.

people-in-arms.rationale: He called for arming workers and a general armament and opposed a standing army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He saw peasants as attached to land and harder to win over than workers.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No source records a position on reunifying nations divided by outside powers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He held education the key to freedom and wanted universal education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not addressed; his Enlightenment rationalism would resist it but this is not stated.

death-penalty.rationale: His recorded writings do not take a stance on capital punishment for terrorism or other crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed beyond demanding secular education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: He demands free, compulsory, secular schooling and opposes clerical education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is not discussed in any consulted source.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He wanted religion abolished and clerical privilege ended.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style nonconformity is not discussed; his austere rationalism and revolutionary discipline leave this unresolved.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He proposed abolishing the public debt ledger and rejected inherited debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from his view that equality needs a change in property.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He proposed assemblies after dictatorship but also postponing elections.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from his temporary dictatorship justified by revolution's needs.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: International aid is not discussed; his concern was class relations inside France.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic for him.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; he favored a provisional dictatorship rather than any set procedure for a head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: He wants state financial institutions such as a National Savings Bank under republican control, not insulated from politics.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions in peace deals are not discussed in his texts.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He denies that property can override the right to life and holds wealth belongs to those who create it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for him.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees such as NATO are anachronistic and not addressed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is not discussed in his writings.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He would take the church's goods under state control, end its budget, expel priests and orders and create secular state schooling.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic head of state is not part of his program, which proposes a provisional dictatorship.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from his Jacobin claim that Paris represents the nation.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from his centralism and unitary republic.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He opposed perpetual dynasties and religion alike.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He proposes a progressive direct tax on income and inheritance.

character-from-environment.rationale: His program rests on the claim that education and communism shape free, equal people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He objects to laws imposed on later generations, though his own dictatorship would act outside ordinary law temporarily.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic; his Eternity by the Stars concerns cosmology, not colonization.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He favored republican equality and abolished dynastic and privileged orders.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin and sans-culotte tradition; not stated.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed in any consulted source.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He did not describe life after the revolution in this detail.

land-redistribution.rationale: He rejects dividing land among individuals as letting inequality return and would favor association instead.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not discussed in his writings.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He wanted religion abolished and clergy expelled, so punishing apostasy is the reverse of his view.

women-must-cover.rationale: He opposed clerical authority; the question is not discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary unions are not discussed; his financial plans were national.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: His loyalty was to the French republic.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus struggle for rights is not a question his texts address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Kingston archive says he held that action should be driven by conscious collective will, not economic development or other deeper forces.

ban-cartels.rationale: He sought to abolish capital's power altogether rather than to restore competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts are not discussed; his financial proposals concern abolishing the public debt ledger.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He wanted to dissolve the magistracy for arbitrators and juries and would not let courts block the revolution.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The archive notes his sexism; no view on parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are not discussed in his writings.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade agreements with binding standards are anachronistic for him.

moral-incentives.rationale: His emphasis on reasoned common purpose and education suggests it; not stated.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Blanquism is the view that a small, secretive, organised group can seize power by coup without waiting for mass movements.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He argues that inheritance of land and capital entrenches an idle aristocracy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The framing of school history is not discussed apart from his demand for secular, rational instruction.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule of advanced over less advanced societies is not discussed; no source records his view on colonial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: He wanted mandatory state schooling and was a Jacobin patriot, but patriotism in curricula is not stated.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are anachronistic for him.

public-money-creation.rationale: He proposed a state National Savings Bank and public control of finance.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He saw the owner-worker relation as organised war needing one side to yield.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence over former imperial regions is not discussed in his writings.

delink-world-market.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not discussed; his analysis is domestic.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: He held that workers create everything and own nothing, with no suggestion of shared profits.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He held equality to be the limit to freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He objects to laws binding later generations.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaties are not discussed in any consulted source.

elective-rulers.rationale: He swore men to the Republic, but his own program postponed elections.

minority-veto.rationale: His organisation demanded obedience to the commander-in-chief.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He organized insurrection against governments he regarded as illegitimate.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He feared elected assemblies would undo the revolution; he did not address legislative supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not found in his writings or the scholarship on him.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in any consulted source.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He saw owners as an idle minority taking workers' product, so charity from them is no remedy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He considered neutrality the gravest political failing.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He held that the church and a controlled press maintain ignorance underpinning oppression.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: He describes a clergy spreading ignorance with state support, which wins the masses over for the old order.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-system theories postdate him; his analysis is of owners and workers within a country.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for public office by birth is not discussed in his texts.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations between national communist parties postdate him.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Foreign aid and development finance are not discussed in his writings.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demands for lost territory are not discussed; no source records a Blanquist irredentist claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism postdates him by decades, so there is no recorded position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; a revolutionary communist would resist equating them.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian outlook; not discussed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Debates over monuments are anachronistic; no source gives his view.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The archive notes his sexism; no view recorded.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is anachronistic and not discussed in his writings.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He would disband the existing army and replace it by a national army and general armament.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid care work is not discussed in his texts; the archive notes only his sexism.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is not discussed; he criticized obligations imposed on later generations but not parental ones.

office-by-exam.rationale: He favored a body of teachers for education but did not discuss civil service.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign acquisitions of firms are anachronistic for him.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in any consulted source.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from his Jacobin sans-culotte tradition; his own organisation was hierarchical.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: He opposed individual capital and favored state financial institutions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: He argues land is an inert instrument and equality requires association replacing individual property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not discussed; he distrusted elected assemblies after a revolution.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from Jacobin centralism and compulsory national schooling.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land is not discussed in his writings.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is a modern legal concept with no Blanquist position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He criticized market logic and praised thought over dexterity; modest inference.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Support for foreign insurgents is not discussed in his texts.

corporate-influence.rationale: He held that owners of capital dominate society.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs is anachronistic for him.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth incentives are not discussed in his writings.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in any consulted source.

job-guarantee.rationale: Early measures would require heads of industry to keep their workforce, showing concern for employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic-peace theory is not discussed in his texts.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: His organization demanded obedience to its own commander.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from revolutionary universalism; not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in his writings.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The legal institution of marriage is not discussed in his texts.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not discussed in his writings.

local-production.rationale: Local sourcing of food and goods is not discussed; his economic writing concerns ownership.

informal-organisation.rationale: Blanquism uses small trusted conspiratorial groups but with a strict disciplined hierarchy, so it is split on this wording.

religious-nation.rationale: He wanted religion abolished and priests expelled.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: He would respect small and medium property and not attack property directly.

defeat-communism.rationale: He calls communism necessary and the future of society, so an adherent would want it advanced rather than defeated.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He demanded state-run secular schooling and opposed independent schools.

religion-illusion.rationale: He treated religion as the ideological support of the old order, to fade with universal education, not as consolation for suffering.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He saw property as based on force and fraud; credit for historical progress is not discussed.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The archive notes his sexism; no view recorded.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not discussed in any consulted source.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not a Blanquist theme.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed in his writings.

cooperative-communities.rationale: He favored association but through a national and Parisian-led state rather than small communities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third course is excluded because he held that communism by association, reached through universal education, is the necessary outcome.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not discussed in his texts.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sexual-conduct law is not discussed in any consulted source.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His temporary dictatorship would suppress counter-revolution.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He wanted religion abolished and had no sympathy for punishing its critics.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from his atheism and rejection of religion in politics.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He sought to expel the clergy, not to rule by religion.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The archive stresses collective participation and mass education toward self-government.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a late-20th-century idea with no recorded Blanquist position.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender-identity law is anachronistic for him.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in his writings.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He rejected the middle way and neutrality, treating politics as war between classes.

alienated-labor.rationale: He says workers create everything yet own nothing, their output taken by an idle minority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He demanded secular state schooling and the exclusion of clergy from public institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment contract rules are anachronistic for him.

social-market-economy.rationale: He sees owners and workers as in organised war and seeks to replace capital with association.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He wanted a national army and general armament.

rich-first.rationale: He holds equality to be the first law of the new order.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power blocs of that kind postdate him.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: He proposed a state savings bank, not mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style conditionality is anachronistic; he only proposed abolishing the domestic public debt ledger.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is anachronistic and his writings do not connect these themes.

property-franchise.rationale: He sees property as based on force and fraud and a source of the owners' domination.

reification.rationale: He described capital as acquiring value only through labor but did not develop a theory of reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He held that a controlled press, with the church, maintains ignorance supporting oppression.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: His program involved a dictatorship acting by decree during the transition.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contradicts equality as the first law of the new order.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is anachronistic for him.

open-government-data.rationale: Open-data publication is anachronistic and not discussed in his writings.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: He opposed religious authority over public life.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Blanqui held that a provisional dictatorship must educate the people before they can govern themselves, so deliberation by lot-drawn citizens comes only after, not instead of, that rule.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Blanqui was an atheist who wanted clergy expelled and religion replaced by secular education, so he would see reinterpreting doctrine as pointless; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Blanqui attacks capital and inheritance as the means by which owners take workers' product and holds that equality requires association, so concentrated wealth is a threat to a free society.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Blanqui opposed a standing army and wanted armed workers, but never discussed sexual orientation; no basis for a stand.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Blanqui was an atheist who demanded free compulsory secular schooling and the expulsion of clergy from teaching.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His provisional dictatorship uses force to suppress counter-revolution and keep order until the people are educated, so abolishing coercive institutions is not his programme.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He rejected the middle way and rule by the revolutionary minority, not guaranteed shares for communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: He held that wealth must belong to those who create it through association and state-led reorganisation, not charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: His dictatorship is temporary and elections come after education, but term limits are not addressed; left neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: He postponed elections in 1848 until the people were educated and relied on a disciplined minority, so open delegation of votes is inferred as disfavoured.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The issue is anachronistic and the sources give no basis to infer a stand; left neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Blanqui was anticlerical and never discussed women's religious office; left neutral.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Blanqui's egalitarian creed suggests equal spouses, though he did not address marriage authority; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Blanqui was a republican egalitarian but the sources say nothing on foreign residents voting; the 1830s-60s French republican frame tied the vote to citizens, so adherents split.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his egalitarian hostility to the property-owning rich and his demand that social wealth belong to those who created it.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Blanqui's demand that wealth belong to those who created it and his communism by association.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Blanqui's Jacobin tradition valued discipline and civic training and secular education, but not drilled national movements; inferred, so adherents split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; Blanqui was a patriot in 1870 yet the question of weapons post-dates him, so inferred and split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Blanqui was a fierce patriot who wanted France free of foreign domination; inferred from his national-defence stance in 1870.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his egalitarian, anti-oppression republicanism, though recognition of genocide is a modern concept.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Blanqui's 1834 text argues that social wealth must belong to those who created it, and his communism rejects income from property alone.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Blanqui led armed insurrection and justified a temporary dictatorship by force against counter-revolution; he did not hold to pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Blanqui's republican universalism sits closer to a civic idea of the nation than an ancient ethnic one; not addressed, so inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The question post-dates him; no sources address it, so adherents split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The question post-dates him; no sources address it, so adherents split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Blanqui honoured fallen revolutionaries and patriots, but his atheism and anticlericalism reject 'saints'; inferred and split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Blanqui was atheist and fiercely anticlerical and held that politics is the struggle of the people against exploiters, not a spiritual one.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the French republican nation-state frame in which Blanqui worked.

culture-before-state.rationale: Blanquism puts seizure of power first, by a small group in insurrection, and spreads education and culture afterwards through the revolutionary state.

god-not-male.rationale: He was atheist and held religion to be an obstacle to emancipation, so concern over how God is described is outside his frame; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Atheist and anticlerical, he held that religion should be superseded by secular education; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Blanqui's egalitarian universal republicanism opposes ethnic domination of economic life; the sources do not discuss minorities, so inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Blanqui's centralised French republican state, which favours unified administration over ethnic units.

missingStatements.text: Free, universal, secular education must come before a society can be organised on egalitarian or communist lines.
missingStatements.rationale: Blanqui writes that universal education without communism and communism without universal education are equally impossible, and demands free compulsory secular schooling.
missingStatements.declined: A historical-sequencing claim specific to Blanqui; the bank already covers secular schooling (no-religion-state-schools) and revolution, and it separates few other ideologies.

notes: Engels and Luxemburg read Blanquism as elitist putschism that did not count on working-class action; the Kingston archive argues this misreads Blanqui, who stressed enlightenment and collective will. Later Blanquists (Vaillant) were Jacobin and patriotic.
